top3.title: DUST DEVIL (1992)
top3.why: PhilaMOCA screens Dust Devil, Richard Stanley's near-mythic 1992 desert horror about a shapeshifting serial killer stalking the South African wasteland — a film that spent decades in butchered cuts before its restoration made repertory bookings like this one possible. It's the kind of genre deep-cut that made PhilaMOCA's reputation, projected in a former mausoleum showroom instead of a multiplex. Doors 7:00 PM, film at 7:30 PM; $10.

top3.title: Little Haiti Chapter Meeting
top3.why: The Little Haiti Chapter hosts a community causerie on immigration and affordable housing, bringing residents, advocates, and local leaders together to compare notes on two of the crises hitting Philadelphia's immigrant communities hardest right now. It's a working conversation rather than a rally — small, substantive, and easy to miss if you're not already plugged into the group. Free.

top3.title: Shaun Milli
top3.why: Shaun Milli brings a soul voice with more depth than his age suggests to City Winery, ahead of a new album he's readying for 2026. He's framed his own project as a throughline to the soul and R&B artists who came before him — a nod worth taking seriously in a city with Philadelphia International Records in its bones. Table service available; note the venue's dinner-show format if you just want the music.

top3.title: esperanza spalding
top3.why: Esperanza Spalding — bassist, vocalist, and one of the defining jazz artists of her generation — plays an intimate three-piece set drawing from all eight of her albums plus a preview of new material. It's a rare small-room booking for an artist who usually fills much bigger stages, and 100% of proceeds go to PRISMID Sanctuary, an Indigenous- and Black-led eco-cultural nonprofit. Second and final night of a two-night run (also Aug 26).

top3.title: Rustin's Challenge Reading Group
top3.why: A discussion group on Bayard Rustin's overlooked "Freedom Budget for All Americans" — the jobs-centric economic vision from the organizer who built the March on Washington but rarely gets credit for the ideas behind it. Led by Paul Prescod, it's political education in the literal sense: reading and arguing through an alternative to austerity politics, not just another lecture. Free, Rittenhouse Square.

Worth catching for the retrospective angle as much as the usual demos and networking. Northern Liberties: nearest stop is the Market-Frankford Line at Girard Ave, about a half-mile walk.

top3.title: Dekalog: Parts 5 & 6
top3.why: The Philadelphia Film Society continues its Dekalog Special Series with parts 5 and 6 of Kieślowski's ten-part meditation on the Ten Commandments, screening in 4K — a defense attorney's crisis of conscience over a death-penalty case, paired with a teenager's obsessive fixation on his neighbor. Widely regarded as one of the towering achievements in film history, and a rare chance to see it as intended: on a big screen, in installments. Likely at PFS Film Society Center, based on the day's other PFS repertory booking.

top3.title: West Philly Canvass for Chris Rabb
top3.why: Philly DSA canvasses Kingsessing for Chris Rabb, a democratic socialist running for PA-03 on universal healthcare, childcare, and abolishing ICE — retail politics for a candidate trying to prove a socialist can actually win a Philadelphia congressional seat. No experience needed; new canvassers are paired with a partner, and there's a debrief after. Kingsessing, Southwest Philadelphia — bus-served (routes 17/64), no nearby rail station.

top3.title: Cure
top3.why: Kiyoshi Kurosawa's Cure (1997) closes out PFS's Terror Trilogy series in 4K — a detective drawn into a string of murders committed by seemingly ordinary people under a stranger's hypnotic influence. Kurosawa built his reputation turning modern Japan into a landscape of quiet dread, and this is the film critics point to first. Likely at PFS Film Society Center, based on other bookings under this venue listing.

top3.title: 📍 Offline GPS Unit Workshop
top3.venue: Iffy Books, 404 S. 20th St., Philadelphia, 19146, United States
top3.why: Build a fully offline GPS unit at Iffy Books — a Pi Pico microcontroller, a GPS module, and a tiny OLED display, wired up in MicroPython to show your coordinates and the time with no internet or cell connection at all. It's DIY electronics at its most quietly radical: a gadget that works precisely because it can't be tracked, monetized, or bricked by a company's server going dark. Requires a ~$40-50 parts kit, purchased separately.

top3.title: Prisoner Correspondence Project: Initial Interest Meeting
top3.venue: Wooden Shoe Books, 704 South St, Philadelphia, PA 19147
top3.why: Wooden Shoe Books hosts an initial interest meeting for a prisoner-correspondence penpal program serving LGBTQIA+ people currently incarcerated. No commitment required to attend — organizers will explain how the program works, and there's an option to write one-time letters to specific political prisoners if a long-term penpal relationship isn't feasible. Quiet, unglamorous solidarity work of exactly the kind that's easy to walk past.

top3.title: Froggy, PLEASURE DEATH & The Angies
top3.why: Froggy — a Philly queer punk power trio who started as teenagers in 2020 — headline with New York's PLEASURE DEATH, a queer heavy-grunge duo, and The Angies. Froggy write punchy, melodic songs about the mundane and absurd parts of growing up (711 nachos gets a shoutout), channeling L7, Bikini Kill, and The Dead Milkmen without imitating them. top3.title: August 2026: ASL Guide-Led Tour and Discussion

A rare instance of an already-thoughtful historic-site tour built for genuine accessibility from the ground up. Fairmount — reachable via SEPTA bus (routes 7/32/48), roughly a 15-20 minute walk from the Spring Garden stop on the Broad Street Line.
